title: WITH (CTEs): breaking big queries into steps
explanation: As queries get bigger, they get hard to read. WITH lets you build them in steps. You give a mini query a name, then use that name like a table. This is called a CTE (Common Table Expression), but think of it as a 'temporary table with a name'. The pattern is: WITH name AS ( your query ), then your main query uses FROM name. Real analysts use CTEs constantly because they make long queries easy to follow, step by step. You can even make several, separated by commas.

example.code:
WITH free_games AS (
  SELECT title, genre
  FROM games
  WHERE price = 0
)
SELECT title
FROM free_games
WHERE genre = 'Shooter';

lines.explain: Start a named step called free_games.
Inside the step: pick the title and genre...
Close the step. Now free_games works like a small table.
The main query: show the title...
...from our named step, as if it were a real table.

tasks.prompt: Make a CTE called cheap_games with the title and price of games under 30. Then show everything from cheap_games.
tasks.answer: WITH cheap_games AS (SELECT title, price FROM games WHERE price < 30) SELECT * FROM cheap_games;
hints: Start with WITH cheap_games AS ( ... ), then write SELECT * FROM cheap_games.
WITH cheap_games AS (SELECT title, price FROM games WHERE price < 30) SELECT * FROM cheap_games;

solution_lines.explain: Start a named step called cheap_games.

solution_lines.line: SELECT title, price FROM games WHERE price < 30
solution_lines.explain: Inside it: games under 30, with their title and price.
Close the step.
Show everything from the named step.

tasks.prompt: Make a CTE called genre_counts that counts games per genre (call the count num_games). Then show only the genres with 2 or more games.
tasks.answer: WITH genre_counts AS (SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games GROUP BY genre) SELECT genre, num_games FROM genre_counts WHERE num_games >= 2;
hints: Do the GROUP BY inside the CTE. Then, outside, num_games is just a normal column, so plain WHERE works!
WITH genre_counts AS (SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games GROUP BY genre) SELECT genre, num_games FROM genre_counts WHERE num_games >= 2;

solution_lines.explain: Start a named step called genre_counts.

solution_lines.line: SELECT genre, COUNT(*) AS num_games FROM games GROUP BY genre
solution_lines.explain: Inside it: count the games in each genre.
Close the step.
Use the step like a table.
Since the counting already happened, WHERE works here instead of HAVING.

tasks.prompt: Make a CTE called spending that shows each buyer's username and total spent, rounded to 2 decimals (call it total_spent). Then show buyers who spent more than 60, biggest first.
tasks.answer: WITH spending AS (SELECT p.username, ROUND(SUM(g.price), 2) AS total_spent FROM sales AS sa INNER JOIN players AS p ON sa.player_id = p.player_id INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id GROUP BY p.username) SELECT username, total_spent FROM spending WHERE total_spent > 60 ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
hints: Put the three-table join from Lesson 16 inside the CTE. Then filter and sort outside it.
WITH spending AS ( ...join and GROUP BY p.username... ) SELECT username, total_spent FROM spending WHERE total_spent > 60 ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

solution_lines.explain: Start a named step called spending.
Inside it: each buyer and what they spent.

solution_lines.line: FROM sales AS sa INNER JOIN players AS p ON sa.player_id = p.player_id
solution_lines.explain: Join sales to players...

solution_lines.line: INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id GROUP BY p.username
solution_lines.explain: ...and to games for the price, then group by buyer.
Close the step.
Use the step like a table.

solution_lines.line: WHERE total_spent > 60 ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
solution_lines.explain: Keep big spenders, biggest first.

tasks.prompt: Using the same spending CTE, show the buyers who spent MORE than the average buyer, biggest first.
tasks.answer: WITH spending AS (SELECT p.username, ROUND(SUM(g.price), 2) AS total_spent FROM sales AS sa INNER JOIN players AS p ON sa.player_id = p.player_id INNER JOIN games AS g ON sa.game_id = g.game_id GROUP BY p.username) SELECT username, total_spent FROM spending WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM spending) ORDER BY total_spent DESC;
hints: Mix in a subquery from Lesson 18. You can use the CTE's name inside it.
... FROM spending WHERE total_spent > (SELECT AVG(total_spent) FROM spending) ORDER BY total_spent DESC;

solution_lines.explain: Build the spending step again.
Use the step like a table.
The subquery finds the average buyer's total (about 69.36), then we keep buyers above it.
Sort, biggest first.

recap: You just learned WITH: give a mini query a name, then use it like a table. It turns big, messy queries into clear steps.
